_status: Thursday final: efficientnet_b0 winner, calibrated, canonical oratrace.onnx. Test evaluated once (see metrics.md / parity.json).
resize: whole image squashed to 224x224, NO crop
_notes: S1 bugfix 24 Sep: refer_floor 0.45 -> 0.05 (sensitivity-first). A confident 'Healthy' verdict was the worst failure mode: a case-report image of a large gingival mass got 90.2% healthy (p[opmd]+p[oc]=0.067 < 0.45). refer_floor now gates on p[opmd]+p[oc] >= 0.05 and overrides the argmax, so such images route to 'Suspicious / not cleared'.

Cost (val, tau=0.45): coverage 91% -> 57%; 50% of healthy referred, 8/43 abnormal still missed because their p[opmd]+p[oc] ~ 0. Lowering rf to ~0.02-0.03 buys more sensitivity (5 missed) at ~44-49% coverage; swap freely in this file anytime.

SMART-OM is sketch-art renderings of intraoral photos (see Sci Data 10.1038/s41597-026-06954-5); healthy is 87% of the data. Real photographic lesions (this bug) are out-of-distribution -> the model's healthy bias and miscalibration are expected, not a Python/ONNX bug.

The app MUST apply softmax(logits / T) before display AND before the refer_floor check (CONTRACT v2 step 1). The reported 90.2% matches post-T softmax, so the refer gate operates on the same calibrated probabilities.
T, tau final (calibrated on val only by scripts/calibrate.py).
blur_min=45.7 = 5th percentile of cv2.Laplacian(CV_64F).var() on train images (resized to 512 wide, grayscale).
OC (class 3) has no verifiable patient IDs -> kept train-only; absent from val/test (see data/DATASET_NOTES.md, BLOCKER).
Backbone: efficientnet_b0 pretrained (3 frozen + 15 unfrozen epochs), best val macro-F1 0.4329 at epoch 14.
